proposed_from.topic: Exact selective holdout-power design for two-stratum, two-stage enrichment at a prespecified sharp zero-effect null. Use complete randomization within stratum and stage, an independent exchangeable simple-random stage-1 holdout with rho in a fixed compact interval, and an uncentered standardized treated-minus-control recruitment selector with fixed threshold. On a uniform local-pair-spacing finite-population class with fixed positive-margin selection cells and finite jointly realizable Gaussian primitives, optimize worst-cell conditional local power over compact positive alternatives and nonnegative unit-norm cell-specific stage weights. Prove the selected-quantile convexity reduction, Delta=A-kappa*b1 weight-side theorem, all-nonnegative-Delta unique largest-holdout result, certified negative-Delta interior regime, and complete mixed-sign analytic branch geometry. State equality strata symbolically; give tolerance-certified value and optimizer-set boxes generally and unique designs only with an explicit separation certificate. Consumer: continuous-outcome FOURIER-style future enrichment designs using exact selective randomization inference. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Ehrhard convexity makes the selected-score quantiles convex and reduces every above-size optimizing comparison over an arbitrary compact positive alternative set to its least coordinate. In the exchangeable square-root path, a Mills-ratio factorization proves that Delta determines which side of the proportional stage weight contains every optimum; a realizability bound then makes the largest allowed holdout uniquely optimal when all retained cells have nonnegative Delta. A 100-bit Arb certificate gives a legal negative-Delta mixture whose interior design has power above 0.86428621266 while both endpoint continua stay below 0.86304573855. Symbolic equality predicates and tolerance boxes avoid the refuted exact-real zero oracle. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Establish the uniform split-conditional Gaussian and zero-null reference transfer with common finite-population remainder, including random complement counts, studentization, rank stability, and conditional quantile transfer. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently verify the Ehrhard-to-quantile single-crossing reduction, then prove the reference approximation on one bounded nonproportional baseline family; pivot if additional population assumptions are necessary. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest result is Freidling, Zhao, and Gao's exact selective randomization test: Proposition 1 gives selective type-I control, Proposition 2 gives the conditional reference representation and computability under imputability, and Section 5 poses holdout and statistic design. The closest design comparator is Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu's sparse-program optimization, which is model-based, discretized, and targeted to expected sample size and familywise error rather than conditional randomization-power geometry. The kernel separates the fixed baseline array, the family of true local-alternative sampling laws \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), and, for each \(\rho\)-indexed dataset, its exact combinatorial candidate support, recomputed complete-cell selector, Fisher reference, cell probability, cdf, critical value, and distance. A deterministic sampling margin and a random-reference convergence-in-probability margin license separate shifted-sampling and zero-drift-reference transfers; explicit inequalities derive both centered-outcome and normalized-midrank maximum-influence ratios, and the holdout restriction derives the limiting residual bound \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\), without adding conclusion-shaped assumptions. Cross-stratum product cancellation then yields the scalar selected-power functional. Within that justified limit experiment, selected-quantile convexity has the explicit chord-equality classification \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\iff(r=0\text{ or }c_0=c_1)\), arbitrary compact alternatives reduce to least coordinates, \(\Delta_j\) determines the admissible weight side, nonnegative discrepancies force the largest holdout, an explicit bounded mixture verifies the reference margin and realizes a certified negative-discrepancy interior regime, and mixed signs admit a complete equality-aware analytic argmax correspondence.

seed_details.seed: Uniform split-conditional Gaussian and zero-null reference transfer
seed_details.anchor: FreidlingZhaoGao2026SelectiveRI, Proposition 2 and Section 5; LiDing2017FinitePopulationCLT, Theorems 2 and 4
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Embed the complement selector, full-stage rank contrasts, random complement counts, and studentizers in one without-replacement vector before dividing by the selected-cell probability.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite-population conditional central limit theorems combined with selective randomization, studentized holdouts, and adaptive enrichment found unconditional permutation bounds and iid randomized-selection transfer, but no matching theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Li and Ding because their multivariate finite-population central limit theorem already covers all coordinates.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem is unconditional and does not transfer a null-imputed studentized reference distribution, moving conditional quantiles, or random split-complement counts through an adaptive selection cell.
seed_details.burned_reason: The sole selected angle exhausted its proposal revisions and then failed the field gate because its load-bearing finite-population transfer remained unproved.

seed_details.seed: Exact maximin holdout and cell-specific weight frontier
seed_details.anchor: FreidlingZhaoGao2026SelectiveRI, Section 5, especially the open questions on holdout size and powerful selection-dependent statistics
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace simulated weight comparisons by the exact selected-Gaussian power functional and differentiate jointly through its moving conditional critical value.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing selective randomization inference with holdout allocation, maximin local power, and two-stage enrichment returned no analytic holdout--weight argmax theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Freidling, Zhao, and Gao because they already recommend holdouts and selection-dependent weights.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their paper proves validity and reports simulations; it explicitly leaves the number and stage placement of holdouts and the characterization of powerful statistics open.

seed_details.seed: Quantitative conditional Berry--Esseen modulus for adaptive enrichment cells
seed_details.anchor: ShiDing2025BerryEsseen, Theorem 1 and the variance-estimation results
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Convert a joint permutation-statistic bound into a ratio bound for the selected cdf using a common numerator--denominator remainder and Gaussian anti-concentration.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Berry--Esseen bounds conditional on adaptive enrichment selection found no finite-population theorem with studentization and null-reference quantile transfer.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by dividing the Shi--Ding bound by the selection probability.
seed_details.rebuttal: The numerator includes nonsmooth selection, random counts, estimated scales, and an imputed reference law; a scalar bound cannot control all of them with one remainder.

seed_details.anchor: TianTaylor2018RandomizedResponse, Theorem 9 and its selection-likelihood proof
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the smooth iid selection likelihood by a discontinuous without-replacement cell and derive the smallest margin rate dominating approximation, studentization, and count errors.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for shrinking-margin selective central limit theorems under complete randomization found post-selection nonuniformity results but no enrichment-specific sharp frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the selective central limit theorem of Tian and Taylor.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their proof uses independent sampling and smooth external randomization; the proposed boundary is generated by dependent permutation statistics and cell-rank switches.

seed_details.seed: Weak-null selective Gaussian prepivoting after enrichment
seed_details.anchor: FreidlingZhaoGao2026SelectiveRI, Section 5 discussion of weak average-effect nulls
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Prove conditional stochastic dominance between the heterogeneous-effect sampling law and the sharp-null reference after both are restricted to the same recruitment cell.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found Wu--Ding studentization and Cohen--Fogarty Gaussian prepivoting only for nonselective experiments.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by applying Gaussian prepivoting inside each selected cell.
seed_details.rebuttal: Unconditional dominance need not survive division by a selection probability, and the sharp-null and heterogeneous-effect laws need not assign the same mass to the recruitment event.

seed_details.anchor: FreidlingZhaoGao2026SelectiveRI, Section 5 discussion of continuous cutoffs
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Characterize the assignment orbit compatible with each selected cutoff and lower-bound its residual entropy before deriving local power.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found Gao's self-contained fixed-trial selector and Stallard's Gaussian nested-subgroup approximation, but no exact two-stage support-retention frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Gao because self-contained cutoff selection already uses the whole selected subgroup.
seed_details.rebuttal: The destination adds adaptive stage-2 recruitment and asks which holdout schemes leave a nonvanishing stage-1 assignment orbit after the cutoff is fixed.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace discretized stochastic-policy optimization and ad hoc rounding by analytic branch enumeration with interval certificates that retain ties and slack-cell products.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for certified global optimization of selective-enrichment power found numerical design programs but no equality-safe optimizer-set theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A routine interval-arithmetic implementation of Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu's sparse program.
seed_details.rebuttal: The analytic selected-power branches, exact tie strata, and impossibility of universal exact-real tie classification are absent from the sparse-program formulation.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Treat the optimizer as a correspondence and prove graph convergence of pilot-chosen near maximizers without imposing a false uniform unique-optimizer condition.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for pilot estimation of selective-enrichment holdout designs found adaptive splitting procedures but no optimizer-graph stability theorem across equality strata.
seed_details.rebuttal: Berge gives upper hemicontinuity, while the required uniform graph-distance guarantee must accommodate equality strata, slack-cell products, numerical tolerance, and a random estimated primitive vector.

seed_details.seed: Location-invariant leftover-information frontier under finite-population assignment
seed_details.anchor: FreidlingZhaoGao2026SelectiveRI, Sections 1 and 5, read against Chen and Andrews' location-invariant Gaussian experiment
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Identify the finite-population randomization statistic corresponding to Gaussian leftover information and derive the exact regime where last-stage-only inference ceases to be optimal.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining location invariance, conditional optimality, finite populations, and enrichment found only the parametric Gaussian batched experiment.
seed_details.red_team: A direct finite-population restatement of Chen and Andrews.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their completeness and optimality argument is parametric and superpopulation-based; without-replacement assignment and exact sharp-null conditioning change both the experiment and the admissible tests.
